DIS-1: transmit a discovery beacon at a fixed, configurable interval.
DIS-2: keep a neighbour table with node id, address, role, public key, last-seen time and measured link quality.
DIS-3: add a previously unknown node to the table on receipt of a valid beacon.
DIS-4: declare a neighbour unreachable after a configurable period of silence.
DIS-5: compute link quality as the proportion of expected beacons received over a sliding window.
DIS-6: operate without manual configuration of peer addresses.
DIS-7: support an optional configured seed list of peers where multicast is unavailable.
MSG-1: let a user compose and send a text message to a named node.
MSG-2: let a user address a message to the rescue service rather than a specific node.
MSG-3: provide a distinct SOS control that requires a sustained press.
MSG-4: assign a globally unique identifier to every message it originates.
MSG-5: record the creation time of every message it originates.
MSG-6: display the current delivery state of each originated message.
MSG-7: display the number of intermediate nodes traversed by a delivered message.
FWD-1: forward packets not addressed to it towards the destination.
FWD-2: decrement the remaining hop allowance of every packet it forwards.
FWD-3: discard any packet whose hop allowance has reached zero.
FWD-4: append its own identifier to the traversal path of every forwarded packet.
FWD-5: discard any packet whose traversal path already contains its own identifier.
FWD-6: validate the structure of a packet before any forwarding decision.
FWD-7: be unable to read the payload of a packet it merely forwards.
RTE-1: periodically transmit its own neighbour list to adjacent nodes.
RTE-2: construct a graph of the network from received link-state reports.
RTE-3: compute least-cost paths using Dijkstra's algorithm over the weighted graph.
RTE-4: derive link cost from a base hop penalty, measured link quality and recent delivery failures.
RTE-5: recompute routes whenever the topology changes.
RTE-6: treat any node advertising the gateway or rescue role as a valid terminal for rescue-service messages.
RTE-7: select the least-cost terminal when several are reachable.
RTE-8: converge on a consistent topology view within a bounded interval after a change.
PRI-1: support three priority levels: SOS, NORMAL, STATUS.
PRI-2: keep outgoing messages in a priority queue rather than a FIFO queue.
PRI-3: apply priority ordering at every hop, not only at the originator.
PRI-4: order messages of equal priority by creation time, oldest first.
PRI-5: assign SOS priority to every message generated by the SOS control.
PRI-6: display the priority level of each message in the interface.
REL-1: carry a hop allowance in every packet and decrement it at each hop.
REL-2: remember recently observed message identifiers for a configurable period.
REL-3: discard any packet whose identifier is already remembered.
REL-4: transmit an acknowledgement on successful delivery.
REL-5: retransmit an unacknowledged message after a configurable timeout.
REL-6: recompute the route before each retransmission.
REL-7: abandon delivery after a configurable number of failed attempts and mark the message accordingly.
REL-8: detect node failure through absence of discovery beacons and update the graph.
SNF-1: retain a message when route computation yields no path.
SNF-2: periodically re-attempt delivery of retained messages.
SNF-3: attempt delivery of retained messages immediately on detecting a new neighbour.
SNF-4: bound the retention queue by both message count and retention period.
SNF-5: discard the lowest-priority retained messages first when the bound is reached.
SNF-6: report the number of retained messages in the interface.
SEC-1: encrypt message payloads using authenticated symmetric encryption.
SEC-2: ensure intermediate nodes cannot recover the plaintext of messages they forward.
SEC-3: sign the packet header and traversal path with a digital signature scheme.
SEC-4: verify the signature of every received packet before delivery.
SEC-5: discard any packet failing signature verification or authentication.
SEC-6: distribute node public keys through discovery beacons.
SEC-7: use established cryptographic libraries and not implement primitives directly.
LOG-1: maintain a persistent local record of messages sent, received and forwarded.
LOG-2: record status, creation time, resolution time, hop count and path of each message.
LOG-3: record network events: node arrival and failure, route change, duplicate suppression, hop-allowance expiry, retransmission, retention.
LOG-4: store plaintext content only where the node is the originator or destination.
LOG-5: let the user view and filter the local message history.
LOG-6: support extraction of delivery statistics from the stored records.
DSH-1: render the mesh topology as a graph of nodes and active links.
DSH-2: update the topology view as nodes join and fail.
DSH-3: display outstanding emergency messages ordered by priority, then age.
DSH-4: display the originating node and traversal path of each received message.
DSH-5: display aggregate statistics: delivery ratio, mean hop count, nodes online.
DSH-6: receive updates without the coordinator refreshing the view.
